title: Split image filtration and countable successor quotients of an idempotent
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a set and $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of $R$-modules, each generated by an at most countable subset under finite $R$-linear combinations. Put $M=\bigoplus_{j\in J}N_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], and let $M_A$ be its coordinate submodule supported in $A\subseteq J$ [def-trf-coordinate-submodule]. Let $e:M\to M$ be $R$-linear with $e^2=e$, and put $P=\operatorname{im}(e)\subseteq M$. Let $\kappa$ be a set ordinal and $(A_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\kappa}$ an increasing family of subsets of $J$ satisfying $A_0=\varnothing$, $A_\kappa=J$, $A_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}A_\beta$ at every nonzero limit $\lambda\leq\kappa$, $e(M_{A_\alpha})\subseteq M_{A_\alpha}$ for every $\alpha$, and countability of $B_\alpha=A_{\alpha+1}\setminus A_\alpha$ for every $\alpha<\kappa$. Let $P_\alpha=P\cap M_{A_\alpha}$. Then $P_\alpha=e(M_{A_\alpha})$, the family $(P_\alpha)$ is increasing, $P_0=0$, $P_\kappa=P$, and $P_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}P_\beta$ at every nonzero limit $\lambda\leq\kappa$. For $\alpha<\kappa$, let $\pi_{A_\alpha}:M\to M_{A_\alpha}$ erase all coordinates outside $A_\alpha$. The map $r_\alpha:P_{\alpha+1}\to P_\alpha$, $p\mapsto e(\pi_{A_\alpha}(p))$, is an $R$-linear retraction of the inclusion. The $R$-linear map $M_{B_\alpha}\to P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha$, $z\mapsto e(z)+P_\alpha$, is surjective, with quotient modules as in [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. For every choice of at most countable generating subsets $G_j\subseteq N_j$ for $j\in B_\alpha$, the images of their canonical inclusions under this map form an at most countable generating subset of $P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha$. Thus every successor quotient is countably generated. No commutation of $e$ with $\pi_{A_\alpha}$ is assumed.

proof.text: For $p=e(m)\in P$, idempotence gives $e(p)=e^2(m)=p$. Invariance gives $e(M_{A_\alpha})\subseteq P\cap M_{A_\alpha}$. Conversely, $p\in P\cap M_{A_\alpha}$ satisfies $p=e(p)$ with input in $M_{A_\alpha}$. Thus $P_\alpha=e(M_{A_\alpha})$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, induced filtration on P (proof lines 20489–20499); explicit elementary coordinate argument.

proof.text: Coordinate containment $A_\alpha\subseteq A_\beta$ gives $M_{A_\alpha}\subseteq M_{A_\beta}$, hence $P_\alpha\subseteq P_\beta$. The endpoint equalities follow from $M_\varnothing=0$ and $M_J=M$, which hold coordinatewise.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, induced filtration on P (proof lines 20489–20499); explicit elementary coordinate argument.

proof.text: Let $\lambda\leq\kappa$ be a nonzero limit and $p\in P_\lambda$. Its support $F$ is finite. For each $j\in F$, continuity of $A_\lambda$ gives $\beta_j<\lambda$ with $j\in A_{\beta_j}$. If $F\ne\varnothing$, take the largest of these finitely many ordinals; if $F=\varnothing$, take $\beta=0<\lambda$. Then $F\subseteq A_\beta$, so $p\in P_\beta$. The reverse containment follows from monotonicity. This proves continuity of $(P_\alpha)$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, induced filtration on P (proof lines 20489–20499); explicit elementary coordinate argument.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha<\kappa$ and abbreviate $A=A_\alpha$, $A^+=A_{\alpha+1}$ and $B=A^+\setminus A$. Erasing coordinates outside $A$ defines a linear map $\pi_A$ fixing $M_A$, since all operations are componentwise. Invariance implies $e\pi_A(p)\in P_\alpha$ for $p\in P_{\alpha+1}$. If $p\in P_\alpha$, then $e\pi_A(p)=e(p)=p$ by step 1. Thus the specified linear map is a retraction. No interchange of $e$ and $\pi_A$ occurs.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, induced filtration on P (proof lines 20489–20499); explicit elementary coordinate argument.

proof.text: Define $q:M_B\to P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha$ by $q(z)=e(z)+P_\alpha$. Since $B\subseteq A^+$ and $e(M_{A^+})\subseteq M_{A^+}$, its values lie in this quotient; linearity follows from linearity of $e$ and of the quotient map. Represent a coset by $p\in P_{\alpha+1}$. Put $a=\pi_A(p)$ and $z=p-a$. Coordinatewise $a\in M_A$ and $z\in M_B$, while $p=e(p)=e(a)+e(z)$ and $e(a)\in P_\alpha$. Therefore $p+P_\alpha=q(z)$, proving surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, induced filtration on P (proof lines 20489–20499); explicit elementary coordinate argument.

proof.text: Fix the stated generating subsets $G_j$ for $j\in B$. An element $z\in M_B$ is a finite sum of canonical coordinate inclusions. Expand each of its finitely many nonzero coordinates as a finite linear combination of elements of $G_j$. Applying the linear map $q$ expresses $q(z)$ as a finite linear combination of $q(\iota_j(g))$, $j\in B$, $g\in G_j$. Surjectivity in step 5 proves that these images generate the quotient.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, induced filtration on P (proof lines 20489–20499); explicit elementary coordinate argument.

proof.text: Here is the countability check, without a separate union theorem. Choose injections $b:B\to\mathbf N$ and $c_j:G_j\to\mathbf N$, possible by the countability assumptions and choice over the set $B$. Encode $(j,g)$ by $2^{b(j)}(2c_j(g)+1)$. The exponent of $2$ and the odd factor recover $b(j)$ and $c_j(g)$, so this encoding is injective. Assign each distinct image $q(\iota_j(g))$ its least representing code; this injects the set of images into $\mathbf N$. Empty indexing sets give the empty generating set and zero quotient. Together with step 6 this gives countable generation.
